name: When should I consider repairing my exterior stairs instead of replacing them entirely?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider repairing my exterior stairs instead of replacing them entirely?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider repairing your exterior stairs if the damage is localized, such as a few rotten treads, loose railings, or cracked risers, and the underlying structure remains sound. Repairs are often a more cost-effective and less disruptive option for minor to moderate issues. However, if the main stringers or support beams show significant rot, structural instability, or widespread deterioration, a full replacement is usually safer and more durable. Maine Results, Inc. can assess the extent of the damage during an on-site consultation to help you determine the most appropriate course of action, which is a key part of our process to ensure long-term safety and functionality.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair is suitable for localized damage like rotten treads or loose railings when the main structure is sound; replacement is needed for widespread structural issues.
